PR #42 was merged into `main` (merge commit `0ceac69`). The next step is to **rebuild the water deliverables**. Everything in `projects/highland/deliverables/water/` dates from Oct 27, so it still shows the old 102/100/98 in pipe heights and no ceilings.

**Plan, on a new branch `feat/highland-water-deliverables-refresh`:**
1. **Rebuild and check:** run `bm run highland/water build`, which produces the `.blend`, the three `.glb` files and `validation.json`, and confirm validation passes.
2. **Rebuild the viewer and review:** run `viewer`, which produces `Highland-plumbing-3D.html`, the trace review HTML, the review and pilot PDFs and the preview PNGs. Then look at the renders before calling it done.
3. **Re-render the video and GIF:** `render_video.cjs` makes the MP4 and the GIF, but it isn't a step in `product.yaml`. I'd run it by hand and add it as a `video` step so the next refresh doesn't miss it.
4. **Move large files to Releases:** about 11 of these outputs are over 1 MB. Right now they're committed in the repo, from before the Releases rule. Regenerating them means sending them through `bm publish highland/water …` and linking the URLs from the deliverable README. The repo's pre-commit check would block committing them directly.
5. **Update the deliverable README:** add the new heights and their status (ceilings provisional, pipe heights assumed), the "illustrative, not a contract document" line, and a link to the open RFIs. Then open a PR using `ship-deliverable`.

**Leftover file:** the untracked `package-lock.json` comes from `npm install` in the viewer step. I'd commit it in this PR so the viewer bundle always builds from the same three/esbuild versions.

**Two things that would change the plan:**
- **When to rebuild:** if any of the open RFI/ASI items (ceiling drops, pipe routing) might come back soon, it may be better to wait so you don't publish the deliverables twice.
- **Old in-repo copies:** once the large files are on Releases, should I remove the old copies from the repo with `git rm`, or leave them for now?

If neither applies, I'll start with steps 1–2. They run locally, since bpy works on this laptop now.

# Ship a deliverable

## 1. Where it goes
`projects/<site>/deliverables/<name>/` — the folder listed under `deliverables:` in the product's
`product.yaml` (`uv run bm list --json` shows it). Spec builds land in `build/<site>/<spec>/`; copy what is
handed over from there.

## 2. Large files never go in git
Anything over 1 MB (MP4, .blend, ZIP, EXR, GLB, big GIF/HTML):
```bash
uv run bm publish <site>/<product> <file> [file …]
```
This needs `gh` auth (`bm doctor`) and **creates a public download** on the repo's Releases — confirm with
the user before running it. It records sha256 in the product's `release-assets.json`, adds the files to a
`.gitignore` beside them and prints Markdown links. Commit the manifest and `.gitignore`, not the files.
Keep small previews (PNG/JPG under 1 MB, short GIF) in git so the README renders on GitHub.

## 3. README for the deliverable
Lead with what it is and the preview, then the release links, then:
- sources and their revisions; every assumed or provisional element that is visible;
- "Illustrative, not a contract document" if it can reach a scope, PCO or resident notice;
- how to rebuild: `uv run bm run <site>/<product> <step>` and the product README.
All links relative; `bm check` verifies them.

## 4. Verify and hand off
```bash
uv run bm check                      # links, metadata, large-file guard, tests
uv run bm check-products             # if product code changed
```
Branch, commit, push, `gh pr create`; then read CI (`gh pr checks <n>`). Report what was published
(release tag and links) and what was not verified locally (e.g. bpy or GPU steps that only ran in CI).

# Highland — actual pipe geometry, working model

A working model of the domestic-water pipes, fixtures and equipment, with Unit 107 shown in detail. Its plan scale comes from the architectural structural grid, floor datums follow A3.11, and Unit 107 ceiling heights are provisionally derived from the structural set and the unit RCP. Start with the review PDF; it includes a bathroom close-up and the calibration evidence.

**Illustrative, not a contract document.** A model study, not an as-built and not dimensionally verified.

![Unit 107 primary bathroom in the 3D viewer](Unit-107-bathroom-preview.png)

[Fixture connection close-up](Unit-107-connections-preview.png) · [Full-unit view](Unit-107-preview.png)

## Downloads

Rebuilt 2026-11-04. Files over 1 MB are on the [`highland-water-2026-11-04` release](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/tag/highland-water-2026-11-04); checksums are in [`release-assets.json`](../../products/water/release-assets.json).

A [10-second preview GIF](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/download/highland-water-2026-11-04/Unit-107-plumbing-preview.gif) covers the bathroom orbit.
- [Model review PDF](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/download/highland-water-2026-11-04/Highland-pipe-model-review.pdf) — ten pages; the last lists what is checked and what is still needed.
- [Bathroom pilot PDF — two pages](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/download/highland-water-2026-11-04/Unit-107-bathroom-pilot.pdf) — the five fixtures and their supply connections.
- [Interactive 3D model](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/download/highland-water-2026-11-04/Highland-plumbing-3D.html) — download, then open the HTML in a browser. All models and code are embedded.

- [Editable Blender model](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/download/highland-water-2026-11-04/Highland-domestic-water.blend) — building, plant and unit collections; opens on the Unit 107 bathroom.
- GLB models: [Unit 107](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/download/highland-water-2026-11-04/unit.glb), [building distribution](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/download/highland-water-2026-11-04/building.glb), [boiler plant](plant.glb).
- [Source sheets P2.02, P3.02, P4.01, A2.03 and A3.11](Source-reference-sheets.pdf) (unchanged from the October issue).
- [Validation results](validation.json), [video validation](video-validation.json), [calibration and ceiling derivation](calibration.json), [provenance contact sheet](provenance-review-contact.jpg).
- [Proposed repipe strategy — installation and unit-by-unit cutover](../repipe/)

The P1 corridor scene (`p1.glb`, `P1-trace-review.html`) is built by the product but not handed over here.

## Sources

- **RL–REVISED Highland Condos Plumbing**, October 29, 2007: P3.02 riser diagram and boiler piping, P4.01 Unit A / 107 plan (governing for Unit 107 routing).
- **200 W. Highland Construction Plans**, April 2, 2007: A2.03 and A3.11 (structural-grid dimensions, floor elevations), A2.02 (P1 architecture), A7.63 RCP Unit 107 (Addendum 1, May 1, 2007), and P2.2 (September 28, 2006, reference only / separate permit) for the P1 trace.
- **Structural Plans**, Perbix Bykonen, April 2, 2007: S3.7 and S3.8 sections give the R1 slab and band-beam soffit elevations over P1.

## What is documented, provisional and assumed

- **Documented:** building floor datums (A3.11: P1 342.00 ft, R1 353.00 ft); pipe sizes and connection patterns from P3.02/P4.01.
- **Provisional:** Unit 107 and P1 plan XY (structural-grid calibration, ±1% scale, ±6 in local trace). Unit 107 ceilings: band-beam soffit 351.21 ft less the A7.63 drops gives living/dining 102.5 in, hallway 98.5 in, laundry 92.5 in above the P1 floor. RFI 99, ASI 54, RFI 245, RFI 344, RFI 201 and RFI 366 revised these conditions; their responses were not supplied and govern.
- **Assumed:** overhead pipe heights CW 108 / HW 106 / HWC 104 in, held inside the 102.5–109.56 in ceiling-to-soffit band (a constraint, not a measurement; no drawing gives pipe elevations); building stack XY; fixture and equipment envelopes; fittings, stops and wall-side offsets.
- **Unresolved:** the dishwasher supply connection (omitted), the 04 stack R1 continuation, and the exact P1-to-P4.01 tie-in.
- Domestic water only; sanitary, vent and gas are not modeled.

In the viewer, **Bathroom** and **Connections** show the fixture stops and supply connectors, and **Fittings** toggles the representative hardware. The previous [sheet-stack tour](../owner-tour/) is superseded.

```bash
uv run bm run highland/water video    # MP4, preview GIF, viewer preview PNGs
```

**Install new piping alongside the existing system, then cut over one unit at a time.** The animation uses Unit 107 and its bathroom pilot to show installation, testing, cutover, service verification and restoration before moving to the next unit.

Rebuilt 2026-11-04 from the water model's current assumed pipe heights (CW 108 / HW 106 / HWC 104 in). def checks():

    out.append(("python 3.11", ok, sys.version.split()[0], "uv sync", "everything"))

    code, msg = _run("uv", "lock", "--check")

    return out


def main(json_out=False):

- **Not Linux:** it skips the check.
